papers.title: Mindfulness Induction Reduces Cue-Induced Craving in Female Methamphetamine Users.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Inspired by an affective processing model of negative reinforcement, this study aimed to examine the effects of mindfulness induction on self-reported methamphetamine craving and investigate the mechanism underlying this relationship. METHODS: Participants were female methamphetamine users, with 120 in Experiment 1 (intervention: n = 59, control: n = 61) and 107 in Experiment 2 (intervention: n = 54, control: n = 53). Participants in the intervention condition listened to an 18.45-min mindful audiotape to attain a state of mindfulness. Participants in Experiment 1 listened to the audiotape after viewing images of methamphetamine to induce craving, whereas those in Experiment 2 listened to the mindful audiotape after viewing a film clip to induce craving. Experiment 1 used a rating task to measure craving and negative affect. Experiment 2 adopted a pretest-posttest design in which negative affect and craving were assessed using the PANAS scale and craving scale, respectively. Self-reported craving was the primary outcome of both experiments. ANOVAs and PROCESS macro Model 6 were used to test the direct and indirect effects of mindfulness induction on craving. RESULTS: Mindfulness induction had not only a direct effect on self-reported craving but also an indirect effect by decreasing negative affect and then improving emotion regulation in Experiments 1 and 2. CONCLUSION: The findings affirm and enrich theoretical and empirical evidence of the immediate positive effects of mindfulness induction on substance craving, suggesting its promise as a method to decrease substance craving.

papers.title: Psychological First Aid Self-Efficacy and Perceived Ability to Cope With Trauma Among Emergency Nurses: The Mediating Role of Mindful Self-Care Skills.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Emergency nurses are often the first health care professionals to interact with individuals affected by traumatic events. In addition to the high workload and stress inherent in their institutional environment, they may be exposed to traumatic situations, both directly and indirectly, which can negatively affect their well-being. To mitigate these effects, self-care skills may play a critical role. This study aimed to examine the mediating role of mindful self-care skills in the relationship between psychological first aid self-efficacy and the perceived ability to cope with trauma among emergency nurses. METHODS: This study used a cross-sectional correlational design to test the structural model. The sample consisted of emergency nurses (n = 316) working in 6 tertiary care hospitals in İzmir, the third-largest city in Türkiye. Data were collected using a descriptive information form, the perceived ability to cope with trauma scale, the psychological first aid application self-efficacy scale, and the mindful self-care scale. Descriptive statistics, Pearson's correlation analysis, and structural equation modeling using IBM AMOS 24.0 were used. RESULTS: The mean total scores were 133.35 (SD = 21.44) for the psychological first aid application self-efficacy scale, 91.55 (SD = 20.35) for the perceived ability to cope with trauma scale, and 106.66 (SD = 21.01) for the mindful self-care scale. The fit indices of the structural equation model were χ DISCUSSION: The supportive structure self-care skill was identified as a partial mediator in the relationship between psychological first aid application self-efficacy and the perceived ability to cope with trauma. In addition, mindful self-care skills were positively associated with emergency nurses' perceived ability to cope with trauma, indicating that higher levels of these skills are associated with greater perceived coping ability.

papers.title: The Mediating Role of Perceived Social Support in the Relationship Between Mindfulness and Burnout Among Female Speech Therapists in Chinese Mainland.
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: Speech therapists (STs) in Chinese mainland face a severe shortage of professional resources and multiple systemic challenges, including low remuneration, limited career advancement opportunities, and occupational isolation, all of which may increase their risk of burnout. Given the very small number of valid male respondents in the present survey and the female-dominated composition of the speech therapy profession, this study focused on female speech therapists in Chinese mainland. It examined the mediating role of perceived social support in the relationship between self-reported mindfulness and burnout, with the aim of providing empirical evidence relevant to occupational well-being in this practitioner group. METHODS: A cross-sectional design was adopted, and 391 female speech therapists were included in the final analytic sample. Participants completed the Five-Facet Mindfulness Questionnaire (FFMQ), the Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support (MSPSS), and the Maslach Burnout Inventory-General Survey (MBI-GS). Data were analysed using structural equation modelling (SEM), and bootstrapping was used to test the mediating effect. RESULTS: Mindfulness showed a significant negative direct path to burnout (β = -0.152, p < 0.001) and a significant positive path to perceived social support (β = 0.290, p < 0.001). In turn, perceived social support was significantly associated with lower burnout (β = -0.344, p < 0.001). Bootstrapping confirmed that perceived social support significantly mediated the relationship between mindfulness and burnout (β = -0.100, p < 0.001), accounting for 39.7% of the total effect. Further analyses of the subdimensions revealed that the mediating effects of family support, friend support, and support from significant others were all significant and comparable in magnitude. CONCLUSION: In this cross-sectional sample of female speech therapists in Chinese mainland, higher self-reported mindfulness was associated with lower burnout both directly and indirectly through higher perceived social support. These findings suggest that perceived social support may be an important pathway linking self-reported mindfulness with occupational well-being. For this under-resourced and emotionally demanding profession, strengthening multidimensional social support may be relevant to burnout prevention and workforce resilience. WHAT THIS PAPER ADDS: What is already known on this subject Burnout is a work-related syndrome associated with chronic occupational stress and is common in healthcare and education. Speech therapists often work with complex communication, swallowing and voice difficulties, and may face high emotional demands, limited occupational resources and professional isolation. Previous studies suggest that mindfulness and perceived social support are negatively associated with burnout, and that social support may buffer work-related stress. However, little is known about how these factors relate to burnout among speech therapists in Chinese mainland. What this study adds to existing knowledge This cross-sectional study of 391 female speech therapists in Chinese mainland found that higher self-reported mindfulness and perceived social support were linked to lower burnout. Perceived social support significantly mediated the mindfulness-burnout relationship, accounting for 39.7% of the total effect. Family support, friend support and support from significant others all showed significant and comparable mediating effects. The findings suggest that burnout in this workforce should be understood in relation to both self-reported mindfulness and multidimensional social and relational resources. What are the potential or actual clinical implications for practice? For speech therapists, approaches to burnout may need to consider both self-reported mindfulness and the social environment around practitioners. Professional development may include self-awareness and emotional-regulation components, while services and professional organisations may consider strengthening peer discussion, supervision and mentoring to address professional isolation. Attention should also be given to family, friend and significant-other support, as these sources may provide complementary emotional and practical resources. Support-oriented strategies should be evaluated in future longitudinal and intervention studies before being treated as causal burnout-reduction approaches.
papers.journal: International journal of language & communication disorders

papers.title: Cardiometabolic, Physiological and Objective-Sleep Responses to Transcendental Meditation: Secondary Analysis of a Randomised Controlled Trial Among University Staff.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Chronic stress contributes to cardiometabolic risk, and stress-reduction interventions have been proposed to improve stress-sensitive physiology and cardiometabolic health, though evidence remains inconsistent. This study examined the effects of a Transcendental Meditation (TM) intervention on cardiometabolic health and upstream physiological outcomes. METHODS: This two-arm, open-label RCT compared TM (n = 65) with control (access to university well-being resource, n = 64) among Australian university staff. Secondary outcomes included blood pressure (BP), fasting glucose, HOMA insulin resistance (IR), lipids, C-reactive protein, salivary cortisol, heart rate variability (HRV), sympathetic arousal, and a post hoc composite cardiometabolic risk (CMR) score. Post hoc exploratory analyses tested whether burnout, sex and baseline metabolic risk moderated TM effects on HRV, total cholesterol, cortisol slope and IR. Primary analyses were intention-to-treat. RESULTS: TM was associated with a small diastolic BP reduction (-1.18 mmHg [95% CI: -2.35, -0.01], interaction p = 0.036), with a non-significant trend in the endpoint-only analysis (p = 0.064); no other outcomes differed between groups. Burnout moderated the HRV response (p = 0.02), favouring higher-burnout participants and sex moderated the cholesterol response (p = 0.011), with TM attenuating the control-group rise in females, with uncertainty on LDL and HDL. Interactions for cortisol slope (by sex) and HOMA-IR (by metabolic risk) were non-significant; stratified comparisons suggested numerically greater improvement in TM males and higher-risk participants, respectively. Given no multiplicity correction, all findings are hypothesis-generating only. CONCLUSION: TM was associated with small, non-robust diastolic BP reduction with no effect on other outcomes. Burnout may modify HRV response, but this finding requires confirmation in adequately powered trials. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ACTRN12625000134426.

papers.title: Complementary and Integrative Health Approaches for Low Back Pain in Veterans: A Narrative Review.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Chronic low back pain (cLBP) is the most prevalent chronic pain condition among veterans, contributing to disability, reduced quality of life, and opioid dependence. Complementary and integrative health (CIH) approaches offer evidence-based, non-pharmacological alternatives that may improve pain management, enhance patient satisfaction, lower healthcare costs, and reduce opioid dependence. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The objective of the study was to synthesize current evidence on CIH approaches for veterans with cLBP, evaluate their impact on pain, function, and well-being, and identify implications for policy, health system implementation, and future research. The key questions of the study included: what is the effectiveness of CIH modalities in reducing cLBP intensity among veterans, what are their broader effects on health outcomes, opioid use, and quality of life, what barriers exist to implementation within the VA, and what research and policy priorities are needed to optimize veteran-centered CIH care? A narrative synthesis of peer-reviewed literature published between 2010 and 2025 was conducted, prioritizing studies specific to veterans and incorporating systematic reviews, randomized controlled trials, observational studies, and evidence maps. A patient-centered, biopsychosocial, and whole-health framework guided the analysis. RESULTS: Evidence for CIH in veterans remains limited compared to that in civilian populations, but it demonstrates promise. Battlefield acupuncture demonstrated clinically meaningful reductions in pain, although yoga, Tai Chi, Qigong, and mindfulness offered modest improvements in pain and functional outcomes. Cognitive-behavioral therapy, Chiropractic care, and massage showed mixed results, with low to moderate certainty and limited durability. Multimodal approaches integrating CIH with conventional care have demonstrated the strongest outcomes, including reduced opioid prescriptions, improved coping, and potential cost savings. Barriers to care include provider shortages, administrative challenges, and uneven access across facilities. CONCLUSIONS: CIH approaches represent patient-centered and holistic strategies with the potential to reduce pain, enhance function, and mitigate opioid reliance among veterans with cLBP. Broader, standardized implementation and veteran-specific trials are necessary to strengthen the evidence base and guide the sustainable integration of this approach into the VA health system.

papers.title: Dimensions of Consciousness in Organisms.
papers.abstract: Consciousness research has traditionally focused on neural systems and has often treated consciousness as a late evolutionary innovation associated with complex brains. However, accumulating evidence from unicellular organisms, plants, and diverse animal taxa suggests that cognition and consciousness may be more broadly distributed across life. We propose a multidimensional framework of consciousness grounded in the Cellular Basis of Consciousness (CBC) theory and the concepts of the cellular senome and the multicellular N-space Episenome. Six universal dimensions of consciousness are identified and examined across biological scales: state, awareness, memory, attention, perception, and action. We argue that these dimensions are not independent faculties but interdependent manifestations of a unified informational architecture. The senome, conceived as the totality of a cell's sensory experiences and bioelectrical interactions, continuously integrates internal and external information to maintain self-referential awareness and adaptive competence. In multicellular organisms, overlapping individual cellular senomes form a supracellular N-space episenome, a collective informational space-time matrix that coordinates organism-wide cognition and behavior to effect seamless holobionts. Within this framework, organismal consciousness is localized not only to nervous systems but represents the collective cellular interactions of organism-wide informational systems that sense, remember, attend, perceive, and act in manner allowing survival and evolution. In this senomically-based consciousness framework, evolution is viewed as the progressive elaboration of these fundamental dimensions rather than the origin of entirely novel conscious faculties. This multidimensional perspective provides a unified conceptual framework for investigating consciousness across all living systems and offers new directions for empirical and theoretical research into the origins, mechanisms, and evolutionary trajectory of conscious experience.

papers.title: Gay Fathers, Triplet Children: Trifecta Perfecta; Tribute to Dr Alec Roy / Twin Research Reviews: Twin Study of Dog Ownership; Twinning Rates in Awassi Ewes; MZ Male Twins with Mitochondrial Encephalomyopathy; Twin Study of Meditation / Human Interest Stories: Twins with Unrelated Parental Sets; Twins Born in Different Years; Valedictorian-Salutatorian Pair; Annual Twins Days Festival; FBI Identical Twin Identification Dilemmas; Identical Twin Doctors.
papers.abstract: The main feature of this essay concerns a dizygotic triplet set born to a gay male couple. In vitro fertilization (IVF), using egg donation and surrogacy, is becoming a more common method of choice for same-sex male couples wishing to have families. This story is followed by a tribute to a late colleague, Dr Alec Roy. The next section presents twin research reviews of dog ownership, twinning rates in Awassi ewes, monozygotic male twins with mitochondrial encephalomyopathy, and a novel twin study of meditation. Several human-interest items capture other informative aspects of twinship. They include twins with unrelated biological parents, twins born in different years, a valedictorian-salutatorian pair; highlights from the Annual Twins Days Festival, an FBI identical twin identification dilemma, and a pair of identical twin doctors.

papers.title: Psychopharmacologic and Behavioral Interventions in Inducible Laryngeal Obstruction: A Psychosomatic Interface Between Psychiatry and Pulmonary Medicine.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Inducible laryngeal obstruction (ILO), historically referred to as paradoxical vocal fold motion (PVFM) or vocal cord dysfunction (VCD), is a functional upper airway disorder characterized by inappropriate adduction of the vocal folds during inspiration. ILO frequently mimics asthma and represents an important psychosomatic interface between psychiatry and pulmonary medicine. Psychiatric comorbidity is common and may contribute to symptom amplification, autonomic dysregulation, and impaired quality of life. METHODS: This narrative review synthesizes case series, retrospective analyses, cohort studies, clinical guidelines, and conceptual literature published primarily between 2000 and 2025 addressing the epidemiology, pathophysiology, diagnosis, psychiatric comorbidity, psychopharmacologic management, and behavioral treatment of ILO. RESULTS: ILO demonstrates substantial psychiatric comorbidity, particularly anxiety disorders, panic symptoms, depression, and posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD). Speech-language pathology (SLP)-based respiratory retraining remains the cornerstone of treatment and is associated with significant symptom improvement in many patients. Behavioral interventions, including cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), mindfulness-based interventions, and trauma-focused psychotherapy, may provide additional benefit in selected individuals. Psychopharmacologic interventions, particularly low-dose tricyclic antidepressants such as amitriptyline and selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), may be useful adjuncts when psychiatric comorbidity or laryngeal sensory hypersensitivity is present, although high-quality randomized controlled evidence remains limited. CONCLUSIONS: ILO exemplifies the complex interaction between physiologic airway dysfunction and psychological processes. Effective treatment requires integrated multidisciplinary care involving pulmonology, otolaryngology, speech-language pathology, and psychiatry. Psychiatrists play an important role in identifying psychiatric comorbidity, reducing maladaptive illness behaviors, and implementing individualized psychopharmacologic and behavioral interventions. Further controlled studies are needed to clarify optimal integrated treatment strategies.
